summary:
Astronauts constantly face multiple stress factors in space such as radiation, isolation, & altered gravity. These can significantly affect an individual’s health physically, mentally & behaviorally. If not caught on time, together these stressors can make astronauts prone to making errors which can even escalate to fatal mistakes. 

When deployed into deep space, the connectivity between spacecraft & Earth is slow & limited. Hence, no immediate help can be provided during an emergency. 

Also, spacecrafts have limited real estate, infrastructure, energy & resources. An expansive AI or machine learning model may not be the best option as they need a lot of energy & physical space (think data centers). 

To solve these issues, we designed an autonomous system based on robust mathematical models which would continuously monitor mental & behavioral health biomarkers, perform comparisons with basis data to evaluate stress level, predict error proneness based on stress level, suggest countermeasures to reduce stress level, then reevaluate the effectiveness of the countermeasures. This is a complete, closed feedback loop design which iterates itself throughout the mission. As the solution depends upon mathematical models, it can fit into smaller CPUs, consume minimal energy & won't have to communicate with Earth continuously, thus making the crew & astronauts self-sufficient in diagnosing & remediating issues. We also developed a web-app representing a sub-set of our solution.
details:
The main output of our project is the architecture design we proposed for creating a webapp system which monitors mental & behavioral health. This design is in our slides as well as on the landing page of the web app we created. We created a web-app with a subset of the proposed design because the data we have from OSD-618 is limited. However, it is sufficient for us to demonstrate on our app how radiation, social isolation and altered gravity correlate and increase stress level. We also created an error prediction model which demonstrates how these stress factors cumulatively increase error proneness overtime if not corrected.

Benefits of this project:

- The project implores to establish correlation between various stress markers using simple yet robust mathematical models to establish risk mitigation protocols. These can reduce overall dependency on communication with Earth for deep space missions, thus making the crew and astronauts self-sufficient in diagnosing issues caused by various stress factors and remediate them promptly.

- As the solution depends upon mathematical models, which can be easily run by light weight programs such as Python, this system won't consume tremendous amounts of energy and can easily fit into smaller CPUs.

How it is supposed works:

Here we will explain our architectural design in detail.

Phase 1: Collecting basis data on ground & finding best mathematical model

  Stage 1: Control Variable Data Collection  

- Scientists select a few mathematical models which are proven to evaluate correlation between different variables and predict certain probability.

- Scientists define various variables & biomarkers that can be used to evaluate stress levels. Some of our suggestions are to use vitals collected through Bio-monitor smart-shirt (by Canadian Space Agency), facial and voice stress recognition, social interaction during confinement, blood samples to measure radiation levels, saliva samples to measure cortisol levels, sleep pattern, error logs from mock experiments/tasks.

- It is important to collect this data continuously through various bio-sensors, cameras etc to reduce the amount of logging needed by astronauts. Also, the data needs to be collected at continuous intervals to establish a strong basis data set.

- Data is collected for each astronaut when they go through Isolation & confinement training in HERA facility at NASA. Data may also be collected during other training sessions which may induce stress.

  Stage 2: Training the Mathematical Model With basis data

- Use base dataset as input to selected mathematical data models.

- Curate & establish correlation between variables & biomarkers for each astronaut and use it to establish behavioral patterns. This phase can also be used to test which countermeasures work effectively for an astronaut and curate a library of countermeasures dedicated to each individual.

- Using data collected from all astronauts during Isolation & confinement training, wider behavioral patterns can be established which can be used to predict stress increase during a mission. Risk mitigation protocols can be designed in advance to handle probable stress situations.

  Stage 3: Training the Mathematical Model with Near-Earth Orbital Data

-   Continue to collect variables & biomarkers from astronauts in ISS and feed it into the math models to make it robust. Since the ISS is closer to Earth, this is safe opportunity to train this system with lesser risk.

- This also gives the opportunity to filter out the models that are not as effective. We still suggest having at least two models so they can act as backup for each other if one fails and can also validate the output of each other for critical evaluations.

Phase 2: Deploy to lunar mission & deep space mission

  Stage 4: Deploy model to Moon mission/ Deep space 

- Once the model is robust enough and confidence score increases, it can be deployed to lunar missions and be trained further on real data.

 Stage 5: Model evaluates & predicts stress levels

- Once deployed, based on live data fed to it, if it notices elevated stress levels, it notifies the astronaut or crew. 

- It also signals the countermeasure system to suggest custom countermeasures to lower the stress levels.

- It also signals the scheduling system to adjust workload of an astronaut to allow enough recovery time.

- For risk predicted for crew, it suggests Risk mitigation protocols.

  Stage 6: Feedback loop, continuous monitoring & version updates

-  During &after implementing countermeasures & risk mitigation protocol, the model continues to collect stress related data. It Compares this data to other datasets when stress peaked earlier to measure the effectiveness of countermeasures & risk mitigation protocols.

- This process continues on repeat throughout the mission.

- The model can receive time to time version updates from Earth.

Tools used:

Microsoft powerpoint, vscodium, python, streamlit, github

SI usage:

We used Gemini for coding & deploying web app instructions. We also used it to generate code to clean and organize OSD-618 data for the web app. Also used it to suggest best real-life mathematical models used in research that can be accurately used with the chosen dataset. AI was used due to a small number of people (2) on our team, limited time, and our lack of experience when coding in Python.
